description: ​SpaceTech brings together members of DragonBotz and top students from IFSP Sorocaba into a single team built to tackle NASA’s toughest challenges.
summary:
We developed EarthPulse, a zero-login web application and Android mobile app (Capacitor) built for The Earth Information Jukebox challenge. EarthPulse transforms official NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) and GIBS satellite imagery (OCO-2 CO2, GPM precipitation, GHRSST sea surface temperature, VIIRS Black Marble, MODIS TrueColor) along with live NASA EONET v3 natural events into consonant, real-time music via the Web Audio API.

It directly addresses the challenge by replacing chaotic pixel-to-noise conversion with a structured, musical protocol: sub-bass fundamentals encode global baselines, consonant harmonic pads reflect geophysical regimes, stereo-panned high notes mark regional anomalies, and missing satellite coverage remains silent. Users can explore 2D grids or an interactive 3D globe, trigger screen-reader briefings and haptic alerts, and complete short auditory missions that teach anyone how to decode each sound layer.

This matters because vital climate science is predominantly visual, excluding blind and low-vision communities and hiding subtle planetary patterns that human hearing can intuitively detect.
details:
EarthPulse (created by Team SpaceTech) is a scientific accessibility and Earth-observation sonification web and Android application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Its goal is to turn orbital Earth science datasets into coordinated visual, auditory, spoken, and tactile experiences so blind, low-vision, sighted, and student audiences can explore real planetary telemetry together.

PROJECT LINKS

Live Web App: https://multi-forge.github.io/earthpulse/

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/multi-forge/earthpulse

Android APK Release (v1.0.0): https://github.com/multi-forge/earthpulse/releases/tag/v1.0.0

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

EarthPulse ingests imagery and metadata from NASA Earth Observation portals—including Earth.gov / US GHG Center (OCO-2 global CO2 in ppm and EMIT methane plumes), NASA GIBS WMS (GHRSST sea surface temperature in °C, IMERG precipitation rate in mm/hr, and MODIS Terra land surface temperature in K), NASA SVS (GEOS-5 aerosols and Black Marble night lights), and live NASA EONET natural event feeds—and processes them through a two-part scientific pipeline:

1. Deterministic Data Ingestion and Official LUT Calibration:

Instead of treating raw display pixels as arbitrary brightness, both the Python extractor and browser-side real-time extractor decode RGB colormaps back into calibrated physical units using official NASA Look-Up Tables (nasa_luts.json). When computing regional statistics across equirectangular (EPSG:4326) frames, cos(latitude) spherical area weighting prevents polar stretching from skewing global metrics. Near-black land/no-data masks (V < 15) and transparent swaths are explicitly excluded so unmeasured regions report "No data" and remain acoustically silent rather than injecting false notes.

2. Two-Stage Semantic Classifier and Progressive Harmonic Engine:

- Stage 1 (Geophysical Classification): Analyzes calibrated physical values, Shannon entropy, Canny edge density, temporal deltas, and active NASA EONET hazard coordinates to classify the planetary state across 9 environmental regimes.

- Stage 2 (Multi-Layer Sonification): Maps longitudes (-0.85 to +0.85 stereo pan) across selectable spatial resolutions (8x4 macro sweep, 16x8 regional focus, and 1D Astronify-style scanline) to three real-time Web Audio / Tone.js layers: pure sub-bass (octaves 1-2), dynamic low-pass filtered chord pads, and quantized melodic motifs anchored across five harmonic progressions (sub_abyssal, thermal_swell, storm_drop, nocturne_cyber, and crisis_siren), plus live frequency spectrum telemetry via AnalyserNode.

Users can inspect the planet via an interactive 2D Map, a keyboard-accessible 3D Globe with 18+ searchable gazetteer locations and regional magnifiers, Auditory Missions (6 hypothesis-driven learning challenges), custom image uploads, deterministic 16-bit WAV / Standard MIDI / JSON provenance exports, and a 4-tier English spoken briefing system (55 pre-rendered neural Edge TTS MP3 clips for offline and GitHub Pages playback, an optional live /api/tts server, a custom native Android TextToSpeech Capacitor plugin for dynamic speech, and Web Speech API + aria-live fallbacks).

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

- Science Without Visual-Only Barriers (WCAG 2.2): Earth science dashboards routinely exclude blind and low-vision users or omit data provenance in non-visual modes. EarthPulse gives screen-reader and keyboard-only users identical analytical capability through spoken Lundgard Levels 1-3 narratives, a keyboard-navigable 8x4 / 16x8 grid, accessible Legend & Units and Data Table inspection modals, live aria-live telemetry, and Android tactile haptics (LIGHT, MEDIUM, HEAVY) triggered on severe physical anomalies and EONET hazards.

- Educational Engagement Without Competitive Pressure: Six Auditory Missions invite students and citizens to identify real planetary phenomena—such as boreal CO2 seasonality, ENSO coastal warming, convective storms, volcanic swaths, and aerosol plumes—using exploratory XP and badges with zero leaderboards or public rankings.

- Reproducible Open Science: Every audio export can be paired with a deterministic JSON manifest documenting data source credit, acquisition date, physical bounds, LUT calibration, Stage 1 classification, and harmonic parameters.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, AND SOFTWARE USED

- Languages: JavaScript (ES Modules), Python 3, HTML5, CSS3, Java.

- Audio and Visualization: Web Audio API (AnalyserNode, BiquadFilterNode, StereoPannerNode, ConvolverNode), Tone.js, HTML5 Canvas 2D (2D Map and custom raycast 3D Globe).

- Backend Ingestion and Calibration: Python with NumPy, OpenCV (opencv-python), Pillow, Requests, HTTPX, and edge-tts.

- Mobile Packaging and Native Hardware Integration: Capacitor 6 (@capacitor/android, @capacitor/app, @capacitor/filesystem, @capacitor/haptics, @capacitor/share, @capacitor/status-bar), a custom Android Java NativeTtsPlugin wrapping android.speech.tts.TextToSpeech, Gradle 8.2.1, OpenJDK 17, and Android SDK (minSdk 22, targetSdk 34). Runs directly on Android mobile hardware (leveraging native vibration motors, hardware back navigation, system share sheet, and OS TTS) as well as standard desktop and mobile web browsers.

- Testing and Deployment: Bun test runner (47 tests / 4,535 assertions), pytest (15 pipeline and scientific regression tests), Chromium DevTools Protocol visual audits, and GitHub Actions deploying live static builds to GitHub Pages.

HOW THE PROJECT IS CREATIVE

Rather than building a raw beep-mapping script or a purely generative ambient track disconnected from real science, EarthPulse bridges geophysical measurement fidelity and cinematic musical structure. A global CO2 slice in boreal winter sounds harmonically denser and deeper in the northern stereo field than Southern Ocean waters; missing orbital swaths create truthful acoustic silence instead of artificial filler notes; and hovering or panning across an equatorial Pacific anomaly physically triggers spatial chimes, low-pass warmth, haptic pulses, and plain-language scientific explanations simultaneously. Combining interactive 3D planetary cropping (3D Globe regional rescan) with deterministic WAV/MIDI/JSON provenance turns Earth data exploration into both an assistive scientific instrument and a creative composition studio.

FACTORS OUR TEAM CONSIDERED

1. Scientific Truthfulness Over Aesthetics: Enforced official NASA colormap LUT decoding, cos(latitude) weighting, zero-fill avoidance on masked land/cloud pixels, strict source attribution on every view, and clean matte Neutral Graphite / Editorial Light interfaces with WCAG-compliant contrast (tabular-nums telemetry and zero misleading decorative chrome).

2. Real-World Cross-Platform Reliability: Because Android System WebView often disables or drops Web Speech API and static hosting (GitHub Pages) lacks a live Python backend, our team engineered the 4-tier speech architecture (pre-rendered Edge TTS assets + live /api/tts + Android native NativeTtsPlugin + browser fallback) so spoken accessibility works offline inside the APK and in any browser.

3. Mobile-First Ergonomics and Touch Accessibility: Structured first-fold mobile visibility (390x844) around Layer Selection, 2D/3D Stage, Primary Transport, and a compact fixed bottom player bar with zero horizontal overflow, proper Android notch/navigation safe areas, and native file sharing instead of broken WebView download links.

4. Automated Quality Verification: Validated acoustic synthesis invariants, LUT round-trips, 3D globe raycasting accuracy (< 0.05 deg), focus management, and absence of missing-data leakage using 62 combined automated JavaScript and Python tests alongside live Android APK builds.

AI USAGE DISCLOSURE

Generative AI coding assistants were used to accelerate UI refactoring, automated test writing, and documentation formatting. All NASA data ingestion, LUT calibration math, geophysical classification logic, real-time audio synthesis rules, and Android native integrations were reviewed, tested, and verified by Team SpaceTech.
